selection.rationale: Current revision already contains the accepted trial-fc57bca7b9 (fidelity-gated CUDA-graph replay of the prefill Qwen3Model boundary 7f49ae8c64c12e322632/2441f10600ba127de5cb753c; clean AB/BA ttft 25.28->24.44 ms, gain 0.79-0.89 ms vs noise bound 0.14 ms), so launch batching of the prefill is largely spent and the next lever must be GPU kernel time inside the TTFT window. Measured on this exact revision: the model-level prefill call 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a executes 2145 kernels, 21610.7 us inclusive CUDA (call-resources.json), of which ~15.64 ms is cublas GEMMs (~430 us/layer at ~73% of the 4090 bf16 peak), 826.8 us the lm_head gemv (777 MB of weights at ~93% of stream bandwidth, roofline-bound) and 740 us flash attention - pools with little safe headroom. The remaining ~4.4 ms is an elementwise/reduction soup, and its single largest coherent owner is the RMSNorm family: all 145 prefill-phase Qwen3RMSNorm calls (groups ef1a650b08785209a023 = 72 layer norms + final norm, 92f04768733eb2543f5d = 36 q_norm, 4a79f0c7bb426e51060b = 36 k_norm) each expand the transformers 5.16.1 formula 'x.float().pow(2).mean(-1) -> +eps -> rsqrt -> mul -> .to(bf16) -> weight*()' into 8 separate aten dispatches (verified in calls.json: exactly 1160 aten children - 290 to.dtype, 290 mul, 145 add, 145 mean.dim, 145 rsqrt, 145 pow). nsys kernel buckets attribute ~2.1 ms of TTFT-window kernel time to these chains (73-call series ~1.42 ms for the [256,2560] norms, ~0.69 ms for the [256,32,128]/[256,8,128] q/k norms). These 145 calls share one implementation and one owner, so they are selected jointly as one drop-in boundary: replace Qwen3RMSNorm.forward at the prefill-phase sites with torch.nn.functional.rms_norm, which dispatches to the native aten::_fused_rms_norm CUDA kernel registered in this worker's torch 2.13.0+cu129 (dispatch table verified; fp32 accumulation matches the reference formula exactly on CPU, bf16 differs only by rounding-point ulps, max 0.0078 at unit scale). Decode-phase RMSNorm groups are deliberately left on the parent path so the 31 decode steps and the decode_tokens_per_second goal keep their current behavior. Composition with the installed bundle is positional, not structural: the accepted Qwen3Model prefill replacement captures through current dispatch at capture time, so the fused kernels are recorded into the existing replay; the inherited required calls 2441f10600ba127de5cb753c/e7df98b905ed8aa688d5227a keep executing (capture/warmup invokes the sites eagerly, decode delegates to the parent), and in diagnostic captures where the replay falls back to the parent the replacements run and are observed per call. Diagnostic eager captures on this revision (nsys 66441 kernels, python_runtime 1152 eager layer forwards) show the same kernel content the replay executes, so the fused reduction in kernel count (1160 -> 145 kernels) and kernel time applies both eager and replayed. affected_calls lists all 145 selected-group calls plus their 1160 eliminated aten descendants.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing the 145 prefill-phase Qwen3RMSNorm forwards with the fused aten::_fused_rms_norm kernel removes ~1.5-1.6 ms of elementwise/reduction kernel time (2.1 ms -> ~0.5 ms; each norm becomes one memory-bound pass over ~2.6 MB instead of eight intermediate-materializing kernels) and 1015 kernel launches/nodes from the TTFT-critical single stream, reducing ttft_ms from 24.44 ms to roughly 22.8-23.0 ms, well above the 0.14 ms paired noise bound; decode_ms and the decode goal should be statistically unchanged since decode-side RMSNorm groups stay on the parent path. Risks to be measured, not assumed: (1) numerics - the fused kernel multiplies the weight in fp32 before a single bf16 rounding whereas transformers rounds before the weight multiply, so per-element diffs of ~1-2 bf16 ulps propagate through 36 layers into the K/V cache and per-step logits; the frozen checks (logits atol=rtol=0.02, exact greedy tokens vs the pristine reference) are expected to hold but an argmax flip on a near-tie is the failure mode, and the candidate must carry a setup-time fidelity gate (compare fused vs parent output on the live first-invocation tensors, permanent parent fallback on mismatch), mirroring the defensive pattern of the accepted bundle; (2) if the CUDA fused kernel rejects this bf16+weight shape the op silently decomposes to the composite chain and the measured gain collapses to ~0, in which case the AB/BA measurement honestly rejects the candidate rather than the quality gate.

proposal.rationale: Repair attempt on revision 20b69c256741a0d1d90fc6ccaf090347c2dbb16ef9007bc7486f57c5337e1df6 whose previous-feedback.txt shows the installed trial-fc57bca7b9-param-f71a7c8a CUDA-graph fast path never engaging on this worker: candidate_diagnostics (observations/previous-after/candidate_diagnostics-4123e6d6.json) records RuntimeError 'No available kernel. Aborting execution.' raised inside _capture() at the torch.cuda.graph context, so its prefill site routes permanently to the parent and prefill executes eagerly (quality passed with max_abs_error 0.0, AB/BA ttft 25.28->24.44 ms). With launch batching spent, this candidate attacks the measured GPU kernel time of the RMSNorm family inside the TTFT window: on this exact revision the 145 prefill-phase Qwen3RMSNorm calls (groups ef1a650b08785209a023=73 layer/final norms, 92f04768733eb2543f5d=36 q_norm, 4a79f0c7bb426e51060b=36 k_norm) cost 2657.7 us inclusive CUDA (1415.8/770.8/471.2 us; target-resources.json, rank 0) through 1160 aten kernels - transformers 5.16.1 expands each forward into x.float().pow(2).mean(-1) -> +eps -> rsqrt -> mul -> .to(bf16) -> weight*() (290 aten.to.dtype, 290 aten.mul.Tensor, 145 aten.add.Tensor, 145 aten.mean.dim, 145 aten.rsqrt.default, 145 aten.pow.Tensor_Scalar). Each of the 145 module sites is replaced by a single call to the native fused CUDA op aten::_fused_rms_norm (CUDA dispatch-key kernel verified present in this worker's torch 2.13.0+cu129 via _dispatch_dump_table; output = element 0 of its (out, saved) tuple), called directly rather than through F.rms_norm so the native kernel is selected regardless of composite routing. One memory-bound pass over each ~2.6 MB [1,256,2560] / ~2-4 MB q,k [1,256,{32,8},128] tensor replaces eight intermediate-materializing fp32 kernels and removes 1015 kernel launches from the TTFT-critical stream; the selection's nsys bucket attribution (~2.1 ms -> ~0.5 ms) projects roughly 1.5-1.6 ms off ttft_ms, to be decided solely by the frozen AB/BA paired measurement. Composition with the installed bundle is positional and safe: its lazy setup (3 eager side-stream warmups, then the capture attempt) traverses these module sites through current dispatch, so the gated fused kernels run in the warmups and in the eager fallback prefill that the measured flash-dispatch refusal forces; a stream-capturing guard keeps the one-shot gate (which synchronizes) off any active capture and serves the parent there, so the installed capture attempt is not disturbed. Decode is untouched: the three decode-phase RMSNorm groups (09e7b0fc2126f1aa326f, b95197500c06e85287e3, c540a300f299d89ee800) are not in this replacement map and decode invocations (phase 'decode', [1,1,...] signatures) do not match the framework's phase/signature dispatch for these sites, protecting decode_tokens_per_second. If the fused kernel is unusable for these bf16 shapes the per-site gate permanently routes to the parent (zero gain, quality preserved) and the AB/BA measurement rejects the candidate honestly.

setup_work.build_time: No GPU work and no allocations at build(); per site the replacement closure only captures references to the live module weight (bf16 Parameter), variance_epsilon (1e-06) and the parent forward.
setup_work.lazy_gate: One-shot per-site fidelity gate at the first live prefill invocation (in practice during the installed bundle's eager warmup forwards or the first quality prefill): computes fused and parent outputs on the live tensor and compares in float32 with atol=rtol=0.02; ~145 x (one fused kernel + one parent forward + one allclose) of small [1,256,*] tensors, order 10 ms one-time inside the first quality-mode invocation, never inside measured warmup/repeat runs (state persists in the closure for the process lifetime).
setup_work.memory: No persistent tensors, no CUDA graphs, no parameter mutation. Gate transients are freed immediately (<= ~7.7 MB peak per [1,256,2560] gate: two bf16 outputs plus two fp32 casts); afterwards each call allocates one bf16 output instead of the parent chain's eight intermediates, so per-invocation peak_allocated_bytes is expected flat or slightly lower while lifecycle counters are unchanged apart from this transient. No non-PyTorch driver allocation is introduced.

quality_risks: Numerics: the fused kernel multiplies the weight in fp32 before a single bf16 rounding whereas transformers rounds the normalized value to bf16 before the weight multiply, so per-element differences of ~1-2 bf16 ulp (measured max 0.0078 at unit scale on CPU) propagate through 36 layers into the K/V cache and per-step logits. The frozen checks (logits atol=rtol=0.02, exact greedy tokens vs the pristine reference, +1-corruption negative control) are expected to hold, but an argmax flip on a near-tie is the failure mode; only the framework's quality measurement decides.

The per-site gate compares fused vs parent on live first-invocation tensors (fp32, atol=rtol=0.02, permanent parent fallback on mismatch, exception or unusable module) and turns semantic failures into zero-gain outcomes; it cannot see downstream amplification through the network, which remains the quality gate's job.

If the native _fused_rms_norm CUDA kernel rejects these bf16/weight shapes it raises inside the gate and the site permanently routes to the parent (route parent-fallback:gate-error); the measured gain then collapses toward zero and AB/BA rejects the candidate rather than the quality gate.

Composition with installed trial-fc57bca7b9-param-f71a7c8a: gates never run while a stream capture is active (parent serves those calls, gate retried later), so its capture attempt is undisturbed; measured evidence shows the flash dispatch refuses under capture and prefill already runs eagerly through these sites.

Decode-phase RMSNorm groups are outside the replacement map and phase/signature-guarded to the parent, so decode_tokens_per_second should be statistically unchanged; any observed decode drift would indicate guard leakage and must be treated as a failure.

external_invariants: Pretrained Qwen3-4B weights loaded from the frozen assets path with dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation='sdpa', local_files_only=True, .eval(); no weight modification, fine-tuning or second reference model on GPU.

Numerical policy from common.configure(): torch.manual_seed(20261020), torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'), torch.set_num_threads(4), torch.set_num_interop_threads(1).

Whole generation executes under @torch.inference_mode() with greedy argmax decoding over the last-position logits; logits_to_keep=1 and use_cache=True on every forward, KV cache threaded through the decode loop.

Input construction is exact: workloads.json qwen_inference.prompt rendered with the chat template (enable_thinking=False, add_generation_prompt=True), encoded without special tokens, repeated/truncated to exactly prompt_tokens=256, replicated to batch=1, resident on the context device before timing.
Exactly new_tokens=32 tokens are generated per invocation; EOS early stopping is disabled by the explicit decode loop.

The KV cache is created fresh inside the timed run() (by the prefill forward), never pre-built or pre-warmed in reset(); source-local references (output, cache, generated, logits) stay live through the measured region.

ttft_ms uses the source's internal boundary: sync -> t0, prefill forward + first-token argmax -> explicit 'first-token-ready' torch.cuda.synchronize -> t1; the remaining 31 decode steps and final synchronize still execute inside run().

Correctness scope is reference fidelity only: generated tokens must equal the reference greedy sequence (torch.equal), per-step last-token logits must satisfy assert_close at atol=rtol=0.02, and a +1-corrupted logits negative control must be rejected; no broader accuracy or convergence claim.
Workload dimensions (batch, prompt_tokens, new_tokens) are read from request['workload'] in prepare(), not embedded as constants; the frozen values here are batch=1, prompt_tokens=256, new_tokens=32.
Correctness observations contain only tensors/scalars (input_ids, tokens, per-step logits), never elapsed times or performance counters.
Observations are returned as detached tensors (CPU copies), not hashes or sampled subsets; the framework stores references on CPU.
